Rules: Every word starts with the same letter and matches the shown length. Part of speech is a clue, not a restriction. Green = exact word in the exact slot. Orange word = exact word exists in another slot. Gray word = not in the sentence. Correctly positioned letters inside gray guesses get a white underline and are permanently revealed. In Standard mode, a misplaced letter that exists elsewhere in the answer word gets an orange underline. While typing, orange letters have already been disproven in that position; red letters contradict a known-correct position. Hard mode forbids both and does not reveal misplaced-letter hints. In shared results, a slashed empty rectangle marks a letter re-guessed after that position was already known wrong.
Guess validation downloads a plain-text English word list from GitHub when the page opens; it is not an API call. The prototype answers remain hand-authored. This keeps sentence generation separate from the guess dictionary, as intended for the eventual AI-generated puzzle pipeline. This version is trimmed to 10 hand-authored sentence/image pairs with whimsical reward images embedded directly in the HTML and revealed only after solve.
